solutions.check: 28 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Peer: "I'm sadly what Britain lacks now"

indicators.note: things gone sadly wrong are in disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lord mournfully quoted on Britain's loss of standing.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make "I'm sadly" read as speech; the peer is only letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A description rather than a synonym: the British Empire was dismantled after 1945, so an empire is what Britain no longer has.

clue.text: Cyclops has sex with one in the country for a start

parts.note: the setter speaking of himself: I

explanation.surface: The setter boasts of a romp with someone in rural parts.
explanation.walkthrough: Cyclops is the setter, so he stands for I. IT + I sits inside NATION after the N.
explanation.definitionFit: An initiation is a start or beginning, as in an initiation into a new role.

clue.text: Absolute lousy leader enters contest

indicators.note: enters means that letter goes inside the word for contest
the leader of lousy is its first letter

explanation.surface: A thoroughly useless politician leading a party enters an election contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lousy leader' gives L, which 'enters' COMPETE.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolute and complete both mean total or utter, as in an absolute or complete idiot.

clue.text: Maybe Paris is sheer chaos

indicators.note: the letters are in chaos, so rearrange them

explanation.surface: The French capital, or a celebrity, described as utter mayhem.
explanation.walkthrough: Paris is not the city but Paris Hilton, the hotel heiress; "Maybe" flags her as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Paris Hilton is a famous heiress to the Hilton hotel fortune.

clue.text: Cheerleader's skirt half concealed by belly — a shock

indicators.note: concealed by means the half-skirt is hidden inside the belly word

parts.note: tum is a homely word for the belly

indicators.note: half means only one of the two matching halves of the skirt's name is kept

parts.note: a ra-ra skirt is the short flounced skirt worn by cheerleaders

explanation.surface: A cheerleader's short skirt only half covers her belly, which is quite a shock.
explanation.walkthrough: A ra-ra skirt is a short flounced skirt of the 1980s, typical of cheerleaders; only half its name is used. The A after the belly word is the clue's own 'a', not part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A trauma is a severe emotional or physical shock, so the definition is a near synonym.

clue.text: Cool? Start to smoke joints

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Is it cool to take up smoking cannabis?
explanation.walkthrough: Joints looks like cannabis cigarettes; it is the body's joints.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the hip is the ball-and-socket joint between thigh and pelvis.

clue.text: Trump's habitual situation: "FOLLOWING CORRECT ROUTE"

definitions.meaning: Trump is famously often out on a golf course
the plain sense: heading the right way, as a ship does

explanation.surface: A mock headline says Trump is, as usual, heading the right way.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals mimic a Trump all-caps post, but the joke is that he is usually on a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: One phrase, two senses: the navigational idiom for the right route, and literally standing on a golf course.

clue.text: Bloke, arse that would lead you to the sewer?

definitions.text: that would lead you to the sewer
definitions.note: The definition is a descriptive clause for the noun: something that would lead you to the sewer.

explanation.surface: Some objectionable man is the sort who would drag you into the gutter.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as an insult to a man; the definition is literal, an opening down into the drains.
explanation.definitionFit: A manhole is the covered opening leading down into a sewer.

clue.text: Downfall undergone by our Brian

parts.note: a downfall of water from the sky; the word is said, then spelt as the monarch's term

explanation.surface: Some man called Brian suffers a collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye nicknames King Charles "Brian"; his reign is what he undergoes. Downfall is literal: rain falling.
explanation.definitionFit: A king undergoes, or lives through, a reign.

clue.text: In tears, if trousers strain

indicators.note: the answer is found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Trousers split under tension, reducing someone to tears.
explanation.walkthrough: Strain looks like a noun about seams; it is the verb, to sieve.
explanation.definitionFit: To strain a liquid or powder is to sift it through a sieve.

clue.text: Penis scour involved for group of players

indicators.note: involved means entangled, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A crude note about genital hygiene for a sports team.
explanation.walkthrough: Players suggests a sports team; here they are musicians in an orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: The percussion is the section of an orchestra that plays drums and similar instruments.

clue.text: Balls rotated by mug, subject to injury

indicators.note: something rotated is turned round, so the letters read backwards

explanation.surface: Testicles twisted by some fool, leaving them hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: Ed Balls is a former Labour cabinet minister, now a TV presenter; his first name supplies ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To deface something is to damage its surface, subjecting it to injury.

clue.text: Norm's resistance against a Republican and Democrat

indicators.note: placed against means set right next to, so the pieces are joined end to end

parts.note: to make a stand is to resist
the usual abbreviation in US politics
the usual abbreviation in US politics

explanation.surface: A man called Norm opposes both American parties.
explanation.walkthrough: Norm reads as a man's name; it is the noun meaning usual level. The 's is "is".
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean the usual expected level against which things are measured.

clue.text: Capitol, mid riots — not how Trump comes across

indicators.note: the letters run riot, so rearrange them

explanation.surface: Amid the 2021 Capitol riots, Trump seemed anything but tactful.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is framed as a negative: Trump comes across as undiplomatic.
explanation.definitionFit: Diplomatic means tactful, which Trump is not.

clue.text: Cheat in church is elusive

indicators.note: the answer is found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A swindler hiding in a church is hard to catch.
explanation.walkthrough: Elusive seems to describe the cheat; it only supplies its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal sense: to chisel someone out of money is to swindle them.

clue.text: Links with a wife that might be followed by massacre

definitions.text: that might be followed by massacre
definitions.note: The definition describes the noun: a word that might be followed by 'massacre'.

explanation.surface: A married man's golf outing ends in carnage.
explanation.walkthrough: Links reads as a golf course; it means chain links. The definition points to the horror film The Texas Chain Saw Massacre.
explanation.definitionFit: Chainsaw is the word before Massacre in the film title The Texas Chain Saw Massacre.

clue.text: Hackneyed coverage of presidential debut — "fix!"

indicators.note: coverage here is literal covering: one word is wrapped around another
a debut is a first appearance, so the first letter

explanation.surface: Tired reporting on a president's first debate, claiming it was rigged.
explanation.walkthrough: Fix looks like the rigging claim; it is the verb, to fasten.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: stapling fastens things with a wire clip.

clue.text: One who licks ends of shit Danish bacon

indicators.note: ends of picks the last letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: the final letters of shit and Danish
a rasher is a slice of bacon

explanation.surface: A crude Private Eye image of someone licking off the remains of a pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Licks' means beats soundly, not uses the tongue. 'Ends of' takes the final T and H, then RASHER, a slice of bacon.
explanation.definitionFit: To lick an opponent is slang for beating them, and a thrasher is one who beats or thrashes.

clue.text: Sham medicine? Spot a personal problem

parts.note: body odour, a classic personal problem

explanation.surface: A fake cure for a pimple or some embarrassing private complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: Spot suggests a pimple; it means a location.
explanation.definitionFit: A placebo is a dummy medicine with no active ingredient.

clue.text: Spots Roger in a rough dive?

definitions.note: The plural 'Spots' means spots of rain, collectively the rainfall.

indicators.note: R, IN and A are roughly arranged, so rearrange them

parts.note: R for Roger, the radio word, plus IN and A

explanation.surface: A man named Roger takes a clumsy plunge and comes out blotchy.
explanation.walkthrough: Roger is R in the radio alphabet. Spots is the definition: light spots of rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Spots of rain on the ground show that there has been rainfall.

clue.text: This clue isn't a burden

parts.note: the Christian emblem of suffering, used figuratively for a trial one must bear

explanation.surface: The clue insists it is no trouble to solve.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a Down clue, so it is not an Across one: the definition refers to the grid itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-reference to the grid: grid entries run one of two ways, and this clue runs down.

clue.text: Maybe Capitol attacker from big city, getting stretch? Not quite

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a big Brazilian city

indicators.note: not quite means the word falls a little short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a term is a stretch of time, as of a prison sentence

explanation.surface: Is a US Capitol attacker from a big city facing a jail stretch? Not quite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' docks TERM to TER. The Capitol rioters stormed the US Congress building on 6 January 2021, hence 'maybe': one example of a rioter.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who stormed the US Capitol in 2021 took part in a riot, so such an attacker is an example of one.

clue.text: Drugs abound — respect!

explanation.surface: A party-goer marvels at the plentiful narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: Respect! reads as a slang exclamation; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both nouns mean high regard for someone.

clue.text: Really poor? Not he? Awful balls!

indicators.note: NOT HE made awful is scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone denies it was a man and declares the whole thing rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Awful balls! reads as an exclamation of disgust; awful scrambles NOT HE and balls is ROCKS.
explanation.definitionFit: On the rocks means in severe financial difficulty, like a ship run aground.

clue.text: Hard Dicky's uprising

parts.note: dicky is British slang for unwell, as in a dicky tummy

explanation.surface: A crude joke about an erection.
explanation.walkthrough: Uprising reads as rebellion; here it is a rise in the land.
explanation.definitionFit: A hill is ground rising up, an up-rising.

clue.text: Maybe Labour leader's gone 'creative'

indicators.note: leader's gone means the opening letter of the word is removed

parts.note: Labour is an example of a political party, hence 'maybe'

explanation.surface: The Labour Party, its leader departed, has supposedly turned imaginative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour leader' tempts as the start of a name; it is Labour as an example of a PARTY whose first letter has 'gone'. The quotation marks hint at sarcasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Arty describes someone with artistic or creative pretensions, an informal and slightly mocking synonym.

clue.text: Heavens his load is ultimately endless!

definitions.note: The definition describes the person: the one whose load is the heavens.

indicators.note: the final letter of AT LAST is removed

explanation.surface: A weary exclamation that some burden is finally over.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Atlas was condemned to hold up the heavens; AT LAST loses its end.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlas's load, in Greek myth, was the heavens he held on his shoulders.

clue.text: Direct route of piss: right off course

definitions.meaning: the straight-line path the setter means
the surface pushes a wayward stream of urine; it is only a pun on the letter P against B

explanation.surface: A stream of urine that is going nowhere near straight.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is a pee line: a stream of piss that, unlike a beeline, goes right off course.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: bees were believed to fly straight home to the hive, so the phrase means the most direct route.
